classifications.label: Instrumental drift or calibration divergence between lab and observatory sites
Each instrument measures a different physical quantity; the four streams are not replicas of one another
Measurement noise is high relative to any common signal; true correlations are buried
Environmental or geophysical forcing with a ~6-day timescale is weakly coupled to some instruments but not others
Pendulum and resonator measure physically opposite responses to a shared environmental driver (e.g., pressure compresses resonator, lengthens pendulum)
Observatory site experiences environmental forcing (temperature, pressure, seismic) with ~6-day period that affects pendulum and resonator differently, while lab site does not
Instruments are measuring independent physical quantities (or aspects of the same quantity under different conditions); weak correlations reflect that, not environmental coupling
Measurement noise is high enough to bury any true common signal; apparent correlations and their signs are statistical fluctuations
Residual: instrumental artifact, calibration procedure cross-talk, or data recording error specific to observatory site or cross-type pairs
Pendulum_obs instrument calibration drift or mechanical fault localized to Day 25
Shared ~6-day environmental cycle at observatory site affects pendulum and resonator with opposite sign (pendulum lengthens/resonator compresses under pressure or vice versa)

Observatory site experiences environmental forcing (~6-day period) that affects pendulum and resonator independently, while lab site does not; Day 25 is a local extremum in that cycle for pendulum only
Data recording or timestamping error specific to pendulum_obs on Day 25 (e.g., systematic offset, misalignment with true trial sequence)
Residual: unknown procedural cross-talk, environmental phenomenon, or measurement principle not yet examined

Coupled environmental cycle at observatory site with opposite-sign sensitivity: pendulum responds to one phase of a ~6–9 day environmental cycle; resonator responds to opposite phase or orthogonal component (e.g., thermal expansion of support structure affects pendulum length but compresses resonator cavity, or vice versa).
Instrument calibration or mechanical drift specific to pendulum_obs, manifest as a slow bias accumulation over trials 150–372 (post-baseline period) rather than a sharp Day 25 event.

Lab site and observatory site experience different environmental forcing or are physically decoupled (e.g., different thermal time constants, seismic isolation, or geographic separation); the observed negative correlations reflect lab instruments responding to a global signal while observatory instruments respond to a local signal with opposite phase or independent cycle.
Recording, timestamping, or data alignment error affecting one or more instruments, particularly pendulum_obs or resonator_obs, producing spurious correlations or noise.

Unknown procedural, environmental, or measurement-principle dependency not yet examined; possible non-linear coupling between instrument types or unmonitored environmental variable (e.g., barometric pressure, humidity, magnetic field, power supply ripple).
Coupled environmental cycle at observatory site with opposite-sign sensitivity between pendulum and resonator types
Pendulum_obs calibration or mechanical drift, manifest as slow bias accumulation and elevated noise over trials 150–372
Data alignment, timestamping, or post-hoc filtering artifact, particularly affecting pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation
Lab site and observatory site experience decoupled environmental forcing; observatory exhibits local 6–9 day cycle, lab exhibits independent or anti-phase cycle
Unknown environmental or measurement-principle dependency (barometric pressure, humidity, magnetic field, power supply ripple, non-linear coupling) not yet characterized
